checkpoint.resumeInstruction: 1) Start the next story in the corrected sequence: wugs-s4 (branch-setup -> implementation-plan -> subagent-execution -> verify-completion -> branch-complete -> DoD, same full cycle as every prior story this session). Read its story/DoR/test-plan artefacts fresh before writing the implementation plan -- do not assume anything about its scope from this checkpoint. 2) IMPORTANT, carried forward from wugs-s3/wugs-s7's merge conflict: before creating wugs-s4's worktree, check whether it's likely to touch the same shared functions (_renderGuardrailsSection, _renderOrgGuardrailsSection, handleGetProductGuardrailsView, _resolveAllPendingPrs, _renderPieceContent, _trackPendingPr -- all in src/web-ui/routes/products.js) that wugs-s3/wugs-s7 already modified -- if so, its worktree will at least include both of their changes now (both are merged to master), so a NEW conflict is less likely for THIS story specifically, but any TWO of the remaining stories (wugs-s4, wugs-s8, wugs-s9, wugs-s10, wugs-s11, wugs-s12) that both touch these same functions and are worked on with overlapping worktree lifetimes could produce the same kind of conflict again -- watch for it, don't be surprised by it, resolve by hand-merging both sides' intent rather than blindly taking one. 3) Process patterns proven effective this session, keep using them: dispatch implementer -> independently verify (git log + running the test yourself, never trust a self-report) -> spec-compliance review -> code-quality review -> fix any real finding -> re-review, for tasks with genuinely new logic; a lighter single-dispatch-plus-self-verify pass for pure lock-in tasks predicted to already pass with zero new code. If a dispatched agent hits an API/session-limit error mid-task, check the worktree's actual git status/diff before deciding what's left to do -- don't restart from scratch or trust a truncated self-report. If CI E2E checks fail on first run, check whether it's the documented deploy-group concurrency-collision flake (cancelled, not a real test failure) before assuming a real defect -- re-run once via `gh run rerun <run-id> --repo heymishy/skills-repo --failed` and confirm clean before investigating further. 4) For every pipeline-state.json write: fetch origin/master first and compare against HEAD before writing directly -- if no drift, safe to write directly. Baseline test count to expect: 33 pre-existing failures out of 512+ files (count grows as more wugs-* test files land on master) -- confirm the FAILURE LIST matches the documented baseline (not just the count) before assuming any change is pre-existing.
